chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who does not reckon his speech as part of his deeds, his sins will increase, and his punishment will approach.'

key_terms.حَسَبَ: to reckon, count, or consider as
key_terms.حَضَرَ: to approach, be present, or draw near

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of not treating speech as a deed?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith underscores the Shia principle of *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue), framing speech not merely as communication but as a weighty moral act subject to divine accounting. It serves as a practical reminder that negligence in verbal conduct directly contributes to spiritual decay and impending punishment, reinforcing the link between internal intention and external expression.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who does not reckon his speech to be from his deeds, would be of abundant sins, and his Punishment would approach’.
en.sarwar: 15. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from those he narrated from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘One who does not count his words as his deeds, his sins increase and his punishment approaches.’”
